chunks: Mansur ibn Hazim said to him:
May my father and my mother be for you! Indeed, souls are approached in the morning and in the evening; so when that happens, then who will it be?
So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: When that happens, then he is your master.
And he struck with his hand upon the right shoulder of Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, as far as I know; and he was, on that day, five years old, while Abdullah ibn Ja'far was sitting with us.

key_terms.الْأَنْفُسَ: the lives or souls of people, referring here to human mortality
key_terms.صَاحِبُكُمْ: your master or leader, meaning the one who will hold authority over you
key_terms.مَنْكِبِ: shoulder, mentioned as the place upon which the Imam gestured
key_terms.يُرَاحُ: to be approached in the evening; paired with morning to convey constant vulnerability to death
key_terms.يُغْدَى: to be approached in the morning; here indicating the coming of death or changing conditions

ai.seo_question: How did Abu Abdullah عليه السلام indicate that Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام would be the next Imam?
ai.summary: This narration records a clear indication by Abu Abdullah عليه السلام toward the Imamate of Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام after him. It highlights designation of religious authority within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and preserves a historical report about Imam Musa al-Kazim عليه السلام in his youth.
